summary: This feature profiles eight emerging local musicians and bands whose recent performances in autumn 2023 are building them local and potentially national followings. The acts span soulful vocals, jazz piano, ambient soundscapes, synth-pop, folk-rock, hip-hop, punk-infused country, and R&B/soul/pop. The piece argues that the heart of the arts beats strongest at the local level.
one_line: A profile of eight emerging local musicians across genres, each tied to a breakout performance or release in fall 2023.
key_facts: Sarah Jefferson performed at The Velvet Corner on September 9, 2023; she has strong family musical roots and is a fixture at local dive bars and coffee shops.
Marcus Ellison, known as "M-Keyz," is a classically trained 21-year-old pianist with a flair for jazz improvisation.
M-Keyz became the talk of the town after his performance at the Midtown Jazz Festival on October 15, 2023.
Luna Rodriguez makes ambient and experimental soundscapes with unconventional instruments and electronic synchronization, and headlined the Experimental Echoes Music Night on November 2, 2023.
The Reverb Syndicate is led by Alex Turner on vocals and synth and plays 80s-inspired synth-pop with contemporary beats.
The Reverb Syndicate's viral hit "Neon Dreams" was released in late September.
Janelle & The Chords is a quartet led by singer-songwriter Janelle Thompson that fuses folk, rock, and indie, and sold out The Harmony Hall on October 22, 2023.
Janelle & The Chords' latest album is "Threadbare Tales," becoming an anthem for local youth.
Elliott Moss is a hip-hop artist who produces his own beats; his breakthrough performance was at CityFest on September 29, 2023.
Brianna Hale blends country with a punk-infused twang and performed at the Rustic Melody Club on December 1, 2023.
Theo Martinez mixes R&B, soul, and pop, and made his debut at The Blue Note on November 12, 2023, after which his fan following grew exponentially.
